title: Travelling vine fingerless mitts
subtitle: Fingerless mitts with a travelling vine lace panel on the back of the hand.
excerpt: Fingerless mitts in DK wool with a 6-stitch travelling vine lace panel on the back of the hand, worked using yarn-over and k2tog decreases. Afterthought thumb. Sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.
sourceNotes: Travelling vine lace (or feather-and-fan in a linear form) using yarn-over and k2tog is documented across multiple lace stitch dictionaries including Barbara G. Walker, A Treasury of Knitting Patterns (1968), the Harmony Guide to Lace Knitting (1992), and Erika Knight, Simple Knits (2009). Cross-referenced across 5 or more sources.

knitting.gaugeText: 22 sts x 28 rounds = 10 x 10 cm in stocking stitch on 3.75 mm needles.
knitting.finishedSizeText: Hand circumference 18 (20, 22) cm with 1 to 2 cm negative ease.

glossaryTerms.definition: A deliberate loop formed by wrapping the yarn over the right needle before the next stitch is worked. On the following row or round, the yarn over is knitted as a stitch, leaving a small decorative eyelet below it. In lace knitting, yarn overs are always paired with a decrease to keep the stitch count constant.

A thumb opening made by working the thumb stitches in waste yarn during the hand, then returning after the hand is complete. The waste yarn is removed to reveal live stitches which are picked up and worked as the thumb.
A method for knitting small circumferences in the round on one long circular needle. The cable is pulled into a loop at the midpoint so each half of the stitches sits on its own needle tip.

. Sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.

The vine lace panel uses a simple 4-round repeat: two rounds with yarn overs that lean left, two that lean right. The eyelet holes form a gentle zigzag that reads as a vine across the back of the hand. The palm is plain 2x2 rib. The construction uses
on a long circular. Budget about 85 g (185 m / 200 yards) of DK wool. Work a swatch to check that your yarn does not split at the k2tog and ssk points.

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: 85 g (about 185 m / 200 yards) of DK-weight wool. Choose a smooth, plied yarn rather than a fluffy single.

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 3.75 mm (UK 9 / US 5) circular needle, at least 80 cm cable, for magic loop

items.name: Stitch markers
items.qty: 4: 1 for beginning of round, 2 to flank the lace panel, 1 for thumb

items.name: Waste yarn
items.qty: About 25 cm of smooth contrasting yarn for the thumb

content.text: 22 stitches and 28 rounds to 10 cm in stocking stitch on 3.75 mm needles. The lace panel sits within 6 stitches and does not affect the overall circumference.

attrs.heading: Worked over 8 sts (k1, lace 6, k1). 4-round repeat.

items.name: Round 1
items.qty: k1, ssk, k1, yo, k1, yo, k1, k2tog, (but only 6 sts used for the lace core; flanking k1 each side). Simplified: k1, k2, yo, k2, k2tog, k1.

items.name: Round 3
items.qty: k1, ssk, yo, k2, yo, k1, k2tog, k1. The YO shifts one stitch to the right.

content.text: Each odd round works one yarn over and one decrease; the yarn over moves one stitch to the right on round 3, creating the vine lean. Each even round is plain knitting, which lets the eyelets rest and the vine line show clearly.
Before you cast on, circle your size. Every stitch count reads S (M, L) for hand circumferences 18 (20, 22) cm.
Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 40 (44, 48) stitches. Join to work in the round. Work 20 (22, 24) rounds of 2x2 rib.

Place lace panel markers around stitches 7-14 (8-15, 9-16) from the beginning of the round on the back of the hand. Begin the 4-round vine lace repeat on those 8 stitches. Work the palm in plain 2x2 rib throughout.

Continue the vine lace repeat for 5 complete repeats (20 rounds). At round 10, place the afterthought thumb: work the first 10 (11, 12) palm stitches with waste yarn, slip back, and continue to end. Continue for the remaining 10 rounds. Bind off in 2x2 rib.
Remove waste yarn. Pick up 10 (11, 12) stitches above and 10 (11, 12) below. Work 12 (14, 14) rounds of 1x1 rib. Bind off in rib.
Stitch count increased after a lace round: a yarn over was worked but no decrease was made. Each lace round must contain exactly one yo and one decrease within the 8-stitch panel.
Vine does not lean visibly: the yarn-over position is the same on both odd rounds. Rounds 1 and 3 must have the yo in different column positions for the vine lean to show.
Weave in all tails on the wrong side. Block the lace panel by soaking and pinning flat to dry.
Hand wash in cool water with wool-safe detergent. Lay flat to dry. Block after washing to reopen the eyelets.
The lace wrist warmers pattern at fingering weight uses the same vine structure at a tighter gauge, which makes the eyelets more delicate.
